dok_rationale: Part (c) weighs two bin widths against the coach's purpose, identifies structure lost through grouping, bounds an unlabeled-group conclusion, and defends when the coarser display is preferable.
stem: Suppose a student recorded steps for 30 days. Histograms F and C show the same data with 1-thousand- and 5-thousand-step bins. A coach asks, ``Does this student move differently on school days and weekends?''\par\smallskip \textbf{Priya:} ``Use C. F has too many short and empty bars; C gives the clearer summary.''\par \textbf{Leo:} ``Use F. C combines values that should not be treated as one group.''
first_take: Which histogram is more useful to the coach, F or C? Name one visible feature.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State each bin width and the number of days in F's 19--20-thousand interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Describe F in context, including clusters, gaps, and the unusual value, with units.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Adjudicate Priya's and Leo's recommendations. Choose the better first look for the coach, cite a feature that vanishes in the other display, and explain what its reader could wrongly conclude. State what information is still needed before naming either cluster school days or weekends. Give one specific question for which C is better.

answers.a: F uses 1-thousand-step bins; C uses 5-thousand-step bins. F has 1 day in 19--20 thousand.
answers.c: Leo's F is the better first look: it preserves clusters near 5--9 and 11--14 thousand and the 9--11 gap. C merges these into adjacent broad bars, so a reader could infer one right-skewed routine and miss two possible routines. Neither histogram identifies day type; match observations to dates or compare labeled school-day/weekend displays. C is better for ``How many days were below 10 thousand?'' because its broad bin shows 21 directly.

expectedElements.description: Chooses F or Leo as the better first look for the coach
Cites a cluster or the 9--11-thousand gap visible in F and merged in C
Explains that C can suggest one routine and hide two possible groups
Requires day labels before assigning either cluster to school days or weekends
Names a broad-bin question for which C is more efficient and explains why

scoringGuide.E: Chooses F, cites structure C merges, explains the one-routine misread, requires day labels, and defends a concrete use for C.
scoringGuide.P: Makes the supported choice but omits the inference limit, misleading consequence, or defensible use for C.
scoringGuide.I: Chooses by appearance, treats bin width as changing the data, assigns unlabeled clusters to day types, or cites no feature.

commonMistakes: Saying F contains more observations although both show the same 30 days
Assigning a cluster to weekends without day labels
Saying narrower bins are always better instead of matching the question
